expectations.text: States plainly that the recent-charge lookup is not sufficient
expectations.evidence: The 'recent charge with the same amount' check is a warning-rung heuristic that still leaves the hazard open

expectations.text: Identifies the lookup as a check-then-act race rather than a device
expectations.evidence: It's a race. Attempt 1 hasn't written its charge record yet (it's waiting on Stripe), attempt 2 looks, finds nothing, charges.

expectations.text: Recommends a required idempotency key on the charge path
expectations.evidence: Make it impossible to omit. Wrap the Stripe client so charge() has no signature without a key — a required parameter or a wrapper type that can only be constructed with one.

expectations.text: Recommends a database unique constraint backing the idempotency key
expectations.evidence: Back it with a DB unique constraint on (customer_id, idempotency_key) written before the Stripe call, in the same transaction

expectations.text: Separates the defect from the mistake from the underlying system hazard
expectations.evidence: Defect: 340 customers charged twice. Mistake: the retry path called Stripe's charge endpoint a second time for the same intent. Hazard: a charge can be sent to Stripe without an idempotency key, and nothing refuses it.

expectations.text: Locates the hazard as a system property rather than as a worker bug or human error
expectations.evidence: The hazard was 'optional'; the fix is 'required by the compiler/linter', not 'remembered by the next engineer.' That property is still true after your fix.

expectations.text: Sweeps for other non-idempotent side effects reachable from a retry
expectations.evidence: grep for every call into the Stripe client (and any other payment/side-effect call made from a queue consumer — emails, webhooks, ledger writes)

expectations.text: Treats 'second time this happened' as evidence for pushing to a Control-rung device
expectations.evidence: Why did nothing catch it — twice? Recommends only Control-rung devices, explicitly stating don't let Detection fixes be the only thing added this time.

expectations.text: Attributes cause to the system, not to any person
expectations.evidence: Frames as system design issue; does not blame engineer. The hazard was optional design, not human error.
